prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” — the right roofer depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and schedule. I can help you find the best contractor for hurricane‑rated replacement in Miami if you share your ZIP code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s how to identify a top choice and what to ask.

What to require from any Miami hurricane‑rated roofer
- Valid Florida roofing/construction license (verify on Florida DBPR).  
- Current general liability and workers’ comp insurance (ask for COI).  
- Proven experience with Miami‑Dade County/HVHZ installations and NOA‑approved products (they should be able to cite NOA numbers).  
- Manufacturer certification (e.g., GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, Firestone/TPO) and written manufacturer’s warranty plus a contractor workmanship warranty.  
- Ability to secure permits and arrange inspections (they should handle this).  
- Local references and examples of recent hurricane‑rated jobs (ideally within Miami‑Dade).  
- Clear written contract (scope, materials, wind‑speed rating, timeline, payment schedule, cleanup, lien waivers).  

Materials and systems to consider for hurricane resistance
- Metal standing‑seam or concealed‑fastener metal roofs (well‑installed metal performs very well in high winds).  
- NOA‑approved, high‑wind rated asphalt shingles (Class 4 impact resistant and installed per NOA and manufacturer spec).  
- Properly installed tile roofs with hurricane clips/straps and underlayment (tiles can be hurricane‑rated if installed to code).  
- TPO/EPDM or modified bitumen for low‑slope roofs with NOA/approved details.  
Ask the contractor what wind speed their proposed system is rated for (e.g., 140+ mph), and insist the job follows the NOA installation details.

Questions to ask and documentation to get
- “What is your Florida license number?” (verify online)  
- “Can you show proof of insurance and worker’s comp?”  
- “Which NOA‑approved products and NOA numbers will you use?”  
- “Are you a certified installer for the manufacturer?” (get certificate)  
- “What are the manufacturer and workmanship warranty terms?” (get in writing)  
- “Who will pull permits and handle inspections?”  
- “Can you provide recent local references and photos?”  
- “What is your payment schedule and how do you handle change orders?” (avoid large upfronts; typical deposits vary)  

How to vet and pick
- Get at least 3 written bids with identical scope.  
- Check Google/Yelp/BBB and Florida DBPR complaint history.  
- Ask neighbors or your HOA for recommendations.  
- Confirm they will use Miami‑Dade NOA details and obtain permits.  
- Prefer contractors who offer a clear warranty and provide final lien releases.

If you want, give me your ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll list several reputable, highly reviewed Miami roofing contractors that specialize in hurricane‑rated replacements and are commonly recommended in the area.
